_comment: Del 16 — configuration for Atlas.Api.IntegrationTests' WebApplicationFactory<Program>.UseEnvironment("Testing"). Loaded on top of appsettings.json, the same layering appsettings.Development.json gets for a normal `dotnet run` — see Program.cs's builder = WebApplication.CreateBuilder(args). Two deliberate differences from appsettings.Development.json: (1) AtlasDb points at a dedicated AtlasDb_Test LocalDB database, never the AtlasDb a developer might be looking at with SSMS/Azure Data Studio mid-debugging session, so a test run's EnsureDeleted()+MigrateAsync() (see ApiFactory) can never touch real dev data; (2) BlobStorage:ContainerName is 'attachments-test', not 'attachments', so uploaded-attachment integration tests don't leave files behind in the same Azurite container Del 10's manual testing already uses. Everything else (Jwt signing key, ServiceBus namespace, Redis endpoint) is copied from appsettings.Development.json unchanged: same local prerequisites (LocalDB, Azurite, a local Redis container, `az login`), just a different environment name so ASP.NET Core's configuration system picks this file up instead. Program.cs's `if (app.Environment.IsDevelopment())` auto-migrate block does NOT run for the Testing environment (IsDevelopment() checks the environment name literally) — ApiFactory is responsible for its own MigrateAsync() call before any test runs.
